questions.question: If you connect two identical bulbs in parallel to a battery, how does their brightness compare to when they are connected in series to the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are brighter.
The bulbs in series are brighter.
The bulbs have the same brightness in both circuits.
The bulbs in parallel do not light up at all.

questions.question: When comparing two identical bulbs connected to the same battery, how does the total current through the parallel circuit compare to the series circuit?
options: The current through the parallel circuit is smaller.
The current through the parallel circuit is bigger.
The current is exactly the same in both circuits.
No current flows through the parallel circuit.

questions.question: A student connects two bulbs to a battery in parallel, and another student connects two identical bulbs to an identical battery in series. Which battery will run out of energy first?
options: The battery in the series circuit.
The battery in the parallel circuit.
Both batteries will run out at exactly the same time.
Neither battery will ever run out.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure electric current, and what is the unit of measurement?
options: Voltmeter, measured in volts (V)
Ammeter, measured in amps (A)
Ohmmeter, measured in ohms
Wattmeter, measured in watts (W)

questions.question: In physics, how is electrical resistance defined?
options: It is a measure of how quickly energy is supplied to a component.
It is a measure of how difficult it is for an electric current to flow.
It is a measure of the storage capacity of a battery.
It is a measure of the physical length of a circuit wire.

questions.question: What is the standard unit used to measure electrical resistance?
options: Volts (V)
Amps (A)
Ohms (Ohm)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How does changing the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
Wire length has no effect on its resistance.
Making a wire longer removes all of its resistance.

questions.question: If you double the physical length of a uniform conducting wire, what happens to its electrical resistance?
options: The resistance is halved.
The resistance stays exactly the same.
The resistance doubles.
The resistance becomes four times larger.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, what is true about each individual loop?
options: Each loop can be traced from one end of the cell or battery to the other end.
Loops must always pass through every single component in the circuit.
Each loop is blocked by the other loops so current cannot return.
Loops only connect to the positive terminal and never reach the negative terminal.

questions.question: What does the power rating of an electrical device represent?
options: The total voltage the device can withstand before breaking.
The amount of electrical current that flows through it per minute.
The amount of energy used by or supplied to the device in one second.
The total electrical resistance of the device's internal wiring.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for electrical power?
options: Joules (J)
Ohms
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How can you calculate the total electrical energy used by a household appliance in kilowatt-hours (kWh)?
options: Divide the power in watts by the time in seconds.
Multiply the power in kilowatts (kW) by the time in hours (h).
Add the resistance in ohms to the power in kilowatts.
Multiply the voltage in volts by the current in amps.

questions.question: When a utility company calculates an electricity bill, what is 1 unit of energy equal to?
options: 1 watt-second (Ws)
1 kilowatt-hour (kWh)
1 amp-hour (Ah)
1 volt-ampere (VA)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit that has only one single path for the current to flow.
A circuit with more than one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit that has no battery or power source connected to it.
A circuit where the current must flow through every bulb in a single line.

questions.question: When drawing a circuit diagram, why should you use a ruler to draw the connecting wires?
options: To make the lines look curved like real wires.
To ensure the diagram is clear, with no tiny gaps that would break the circuit.
To show that the physical wires in the real circuit are perfectly stiff.
To indicate that the wire is made of a magnetic material.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the current in the individual branches relate to the total current through the battery?
options: The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current in each branch is always double the total current through the battery.
The current through the battery is equal to the current in just one branch divided by the number of branches.
The branch currents subtract from each other to leave zero current at the battery.

questions.question: How does the thickness of a conducting wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The thicker the wire, the greater its resistance.
The thicker the wire, the smaller its resistance.
Wire thickness has no effect on resistance.
A thicker wire blocks all current from flowing.

questions.question: What happens to the electrical resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
options: The resistance doubles.
The resistance is halved.
The resistance increases fourfold.
The resistance remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for voltage, which is also known as potential difference?
options: Amps (A)
Ohms
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: If a 12 V battery is connected to three branches in a parallel circuit, what is the voltage across each branch?
options: 4 V across each branch
12 V across each branch
36 V across each branch
0 V across each branch
